title: Reading and Improving Code with AI
concepts: keeping an old name as a second name

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked to refactor Sam's stock checker chk(s, o) with clear names and exactly the same behaviour, the AI renamed it low_stock and changed the comparison from < 3 to <= LOW_LIMIT, and said the behaviour was the same. Asha's characterization test for an item with exactly 3 left failed (1 failed, 4 passed), so she put < back and kept the clear names. Renaming also broke her daily report (ImportError: cannot import name 'chk'), fixed by keeping chk as a second name. A later AI suggestion added sorted(), a feature nobody asked for, and her test for the order of the items failed.

changes: The chapter continues Asha's Corner Cafe story: she inherits Sam's old till and stock code, which has short names, magic numbers and no tests.

Each refactoring step is its own small module (till_v2.py, till_v3.py, till_final.py; stock_old.py to stock_final.py) with its own pytest file, so every step's test run is verified and the video can show each version and its run separately. The modules are listed in support_files because they only define functions.
Diffs are made with difflib.unified_diff from the standard library on two verified files, skipping each file's '# file:' comment line, so the diff output is the same on every run.
The failing pytest runs use --tb=no to keep the report short; pytest's own short summary still names the failing test.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
